S5.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S5.text: 1. Descriptive Statistics Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Measures of central tendency are the mean (the sum of the values divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value of the sorted data) and the mode (the most frequent value). The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is robust to them. For right-skewed data such as incomes the mean is usually larger than the median. Measures of spread describe variability. The range is maximum minus minimum. The variance averages squared deviations from the mean, and the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so it has the same units as the data. The interquartile range (IQR) is Q3 minus Q1 and is used to flag outliers: a common rule marks values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR. Population variance divides the sum of squared deviations by N, the population size. Sample
